name: Roll-Top Chafing Dish, 9 L
summary: The workhorse of a hotel buffet line. A counterweighted roll-top lid that opens with one hand and stays open, over a full-size GN 1/1 food pan.
story: The hinge is where a chafing dish dies. Ours runs on a machined stainless pin rather than a folded tab, and the lid is counterweighted so a server can open it with a wrist and keep a plate in the other hand. Everything else on this piece is ordinary hotel equipment. The hinge is not.
highlights: Counterweighted roll-top lid, one-handed operation
Machined stainless hinge pin, not a folded tab
Takes any standard GN 1/1 pan — no proprietary lock-in
Two fuel holders with sliding air control
care: Wipe with a soft cloth and mild detergent while warm. Never use chlorine-based cleaner on the frame.

name: Hammered Copper Roll-Top Chafing Dish, 9 L
summary: The same mechanism as our steel roll-top, wrapped in a hand-hammered copper skin. Food never touches the copper.
story: Copper on a buffet is a decision about light. Under the warm lamps most banquet halls use, steel goes flat and copper holds. The skin is hammered by hand over a form — roughly four thousand strikes per dish — which is also why no two are identical and why scuffing disappears into the surface instead of sitting on it.
highlights: Hand-hammered copper skin, no two identical
Stainless 304 liner — copper never contacts food
Lacquered against tarnish; relacquering service available
Same counterweighted hinge as TRI-CD-101
care: Lacquered copper needs no polish. Wipe cool with a damp cloth. Do not use abrasive pads — they cut the lacquer and the copper will then tarnish in patches.

name: Regal Brass Hydraulic Chafing Dish, Round 6.5 L
summary: A round chafer whose lid rises on a hydraulic arm and stops wherever you leave it. The piece that anchors the centre of a buffet island.
story: A hydraulic lid is a small piece of theatre and a large piece of engineering. The damper has to hold a heavy brass lid at any angle for four hours in a warm room without creeping shut. We use a sealed gas strut rated well past what the lid weighs, because a strut that is working at its limit is a strut that will fail in its second season.
highlights: Sealed gas strut holds the lid at any angle
Cast brass legs and finials, spun brass body
Stainless food pan, brass never touches food
The centrepiece item — specify one per island
customisation: Crest or logo casting on the lid finial
care: Lacquered brass: damp cloth only. Antique brass: dry cloth, never polish — polishing removes the antiquing.

name: Square Glass-Lid Induction Chafer, 8 L
summary: A glass-lid square chafer built for induction rather than fuel. Guests see the food; the kitchen sees a controllable temperature.
story: Fuel gel is unpredictable and a guest can smell it. Induction is neither. This chafer's base plate is a ferritic disc bonded into the pan floor, so it works on any commercial induction warmer and still takes a fuel holder if the venue loses power.
highlights: Tempered glass lid — the food is the display
Induction base plate, fuel holder as backup
Square footprint tiles a counter with no dead space
Cool-touch frame handles
customisation: Matching riser to lift the unit
care: Glass lid is dishwasher safe. Do not thermal-shock the glass by running cold water over a hot lid.

name: Oval Soup Station, 10 L
summary: A dedicated soup chafer with a hinged half-lid and a ladle rest, sized for the head of a buffet line where the queue forms.
story: Soup is the first thing on a line and the first thing to go cold, because the lid comes off every ninety seconds. The half-lid solves it: only half the surface is ever open, and the ladle rest means the lid is never propped on the counter.
highlights: Hinged half-lid — only half the surface is ever open
Integrated ladle rest, so the lid never touches the counter
Insulated shell, cool to the touch on the outside
Drop-in insert for a second soup or a sauce
customisation: Matching ladle in the same finish
care: Empty and dry the insulated cavity after service — trapped moisture is what stains an insulated shell.

name: Mini Chafing Dish, Split Pan 2 × 2.5 L
summary: Two 2.5-litre wells under one lid. The condiment and side-dish workhorse of a breakfast counter.
story: Most of what a breakfast buffet serves is not a main course — it is eight small hot things. Running those in full-size pans wastes counter and wastes food. A split mini lets one attendant refill one well while guests are still served from the other.
highlights: Two independent wells, one lid
Refill one side without closing the station
Single fuel holder serves both wells
Stacks for storage — 12 units per master carton
care: Dishwasher safe. Remove the fuel holder before washing.

name: Double-Wall Wine Cooler, Brushed Steel
summary: A single-bottle cooler with a genuine vacuum gap between the walls. It holds temperature about twice as long as a single-wall cooler and never sweats onto linen.
story: The test for a wine cooler is not how it looks empty. It is whether there is a ring of water on the tablecloth forty minutes in. A double wall solves that permanently, because the outer skin never reaches dew point.
highlights: True double wall — no condensation on the outside
Holds ice roughly twice as long as single-wall
Weighted base; will not tip with a full bottle
Interior finished to the same standard as the exterior
care: Dishwasher safe. Do not submerge for long periods — the double-wall seam is welded, not sealed with adhesive, but standing water in the gap will eventually stain.

name: Hammered Copper Champagne Bucket
summary: A two-bottle bucket in hand-hammered copper with cast brass ring handles. The piece that goes to the table when the order is worth announcing.
story: Copper conducts heat away from ice about twenty times faster than stainless steel, which is exactly wrong for a cooler — so we line it. The copper is doing the work it is genuinely good at here, which is looking like nothing else in the room under low light.
highlights: Hand-hammered over a form — every piece is unique
Stainless liner so the ice water never touches raw copper
Cast brass ring handles, riveted not spot-welded
Two-bottle capacity for table service
care: Wipe dry after every service. Lacquered copper must not be scoured.

name: Brass Champagne Bath with Stand
summary: A six-bottle party bath on a cast tripod stand. Floor-standing, so it takes nothing off the bar and nothing off the table.
story: At a reception the bar runs out of surface before it runs out of anything else. A floor-standing bath takes six bottles and a full charge of ice out of that equation entirely, and it does it at a height where a guest can serve themselves without stooping.
highlights: Six bottles plus a full charge of ice
Cast tripod stand, weighted foot ring
Bath lifts off the stand for filling and cleaning
Drain plug in the bath floor
care: Drain and dry after every use. Do not leave standing salt water in the bath — it will pit the liner seam over time.

name: Ice Bucket with Tongs, Mirror Finish
summary: A 1.5-litre bar bucket with a perforated drain insert and matching tongs. Melt water sits below the ice, not in it.
story: Ice sitting in its own melt water goes from cubes to a single block in about twenty minutes. The drain insert is a ten-rupee piece of engineering that doubles the useful life of every charge of ice the bar puts out.
highlights: Perforated drain insert keeps ice out of melt water
Double wall — no sweating on the bar top
Matching tongs included
Four PVD finishes from the same body
care: Dishwasher safe. Remove the insert to wash.

name: Floor-Standing Wine Chiller Stand
summary: A tableside stand that takes any of our single-bottle coolers to serving height. It removes the cooler from the table without removing it from the guest.
story: A cooler on a two-top takes a third of the table. On a stand it takes none, and the server can pour without reaching across the guest — which is the actual reason fine-dining rooms buy these.
capacity: Fits coolers up to 220 mm diameter
highlights: Weighted cast base — will not tip when the cooler is loaded
Fits any cooler to 220 mm diameter, ours or yours
Knock-down construction: ships flat, assembles in a minute
Felt foot pads, will not mark a floor
care: Wipe down. Check the base bolt at quarterly maintenance.

name: Hammered Round Serving Tray, 14"
summary: A 14-inch hand-hammered round with a rolled rim. The general-purpose tray a floor uses forty times a day.
story: The rim is rolled over a wire rather than simply folded. It costs an extra operation and it is the reason this tray does not develop a wavy edge after a year of being stacked, dropped and washed at speed.
highlights: Rim rolled over a wire — will not go wavy
Hand-hammered face hides service scuffing
Nickel lining for food contact
Stacks flat, 24 per master carton
care: Lacquered: damp cloth. Antique: dry cloth only.

name: Rectangular Butler Tray with Handles, 20"
summary: A 20-inch gallery-rim tray with cast side handles, sized to carry a full in-room dining cover in one trip.
story: We set the handle height at 28 mm above the deck. Lower and a gloved hand fouls the rim; higher and the tray tips when it is carried one-handed. It is the kind of dimension you only get right by carrying a few hundred of them.
highlights: Gallery rim — plates do not walk off in a lift
Cast handles set at 28 mm for a gloved hand
Full in-room dining cover in one trip
Weld seams ground flush and polished
care: Dishwasher safe. Polish mirror finish along the grain, never in circles.

name: Copper Oval Platter, 18"
summary: An 18-inch oval for a whole roast, a whole fish, or a mezze spread. Steel-faced, copper-backed.
story: An oval platter is one of the few shapes that cannot be spun on a lathe — it has to be raised and planished by hand. This one takes a craftsman about five hours, and it is the single most photographed piece we make.
highlights: Raised and planished by hand — not spun
Stainless food-contact face, copper back and rim
Oven-safe to 180°C
The centrepiece of a family-style table
care: Hand wash. Do not put a lacquered piece in a dishwasher — the detergent will strip the lacquer in one cycle.

name: Brass Gallery Tray, Embossed Rim
summary: A traditional gallery tray with a pierced and embossed rim, for lobby, turndown and welcome service.
story: The rim is struck from a die cut in our own tool room. Most factories buy rim sections in from a trader, which is why the same three patterns appear across the whole market. Ours are ours.
highlights: Rim struck from dies cut in our own tool room
Pierced gallery, hand-finished
Lobby, turndown and welcome service
Bespoke rim patterns from 200 pieces
care: Dry cloth. Do not immerse a pierced rim — water sits in the piercing and stains outward.

name: Non-Slip Bar Tray, 12"
summary: A 12-inch round with a bonded rubber deck. The most-replaced item behind any bar, built to stop being replaced.
story: Bar trays fail because the rubber deck is glued on and the glue lets go the first time it meets a commercial dishwasher. Ours is vulcanised to the steel, not adhered to it. It outlasts the tray.
highlights: Rubber deck vulcanised to the steel, not glued
Survives commercial dishwasher cycles
Rolled rim, no sharp edge to a wet hand
Stacks 40 to a carton
care: Dishwasher safe. The deck can be scrubbed; the steel should not be.

name: Hammered Charger Plate, 13" — Antique Brass
summary: A 13-inch hammered charger in antique brass. Thirteen inches of worked metal is the cheapest way a banquet hall doubles its apparent price.
story: Antiquing is a chemical process, not a paint. It goes into the metal, so it cannot chip — and it means every plate in a set of five hundred varies very slightly, which is the point. A set of identical antiqued plates has been sprayed, and you will see the difference within a season.
highlights: Chemical antiquing, into the metal — cannot chip
Hand-hammered face, no two identical
13" leaves a correct reveal under a 10.5" dinner plate
Stacks with felt separators supplied
care: Dry cloth only. Never polish an antique finish — polishing is what removes it.

name: Beaded-Rim Charger Plate, 13" — Silver Plate
summary: A beaded-rim charger, silver-plated over steel rather than over brass — so a scratch shows steel, not yellow.
story: Every silver-plated charger on the market is plated over brass, because brass is cheaper and easier to plate. The problem shows up in year two: a scratch through silver over brass is a bright yellow line across a white table. Over steel, the same scratch is invisible from a metre away.
highlights: Silver over steel, not over brass — scratches do not read yellow
Struck beaded rim
Tarnish-inhibited plating bath
Felt separators supplied for stacking
care: Hand wash and dry immediately. Silver plate and commercial dishwashers are not friends.

name: Smooth Copper Charger Plate, 13"
summary: A plain, unhammered copper charger. The quietest plate we make and the one that photographs best under warm light.
story: Not everything should be hammered. A smooth copper face under a candle behaves like a mirror with a warm cast — it puts light back on the guest's face rather than scattering it. For a room lit at 2700K, it is the single most flattering thing you can put on a table.
highlights: Smooth face — reflects warm light onto the table
Available as solid copper or copper PVD over steel
PVD version is dishwasher-safe and will not tarnish
Felt separators supplied
customisation: Solid copper or PVD over steel
care: Solid copper: hand wash, dry immediately. PVD version: dishwasher safe.

name: Two-Tone Charger Plate, Brass & Nickel
summary: A charger masked and plated in two tones — a brass rim around a nickel well, or the reverse. One plate that works with both warm and cool tableware.
story: Two-tone plating means masking each plate by hand before it goes into the bath, then stripping the mask and re-polishing the line. It is slow, and it is the reason most factories will not quote it below a thousand pieces. We will quote it at fifty.
highlights: Hand-masked selective plating, crisp tone line
Bridges warm and cool tableware in one plate
Two-tone quoted from 50 pieces, not 1,000
Felt separators supplied
care: Hand wash. Do not use a metal-polish wadding across the tone line — it will blur it.

name: Insulated Double-Wall Salad Bowl, 5 L
summary: A 5-litre double-wall bowl that keeps a salad crisp through a two-hour brunch and never rings with condensation on the cloth.
story: A single-wall bowl full of chilled salad puts a wet ring on a tablecloth in about fifteen minutes, and hotels solve it with a doily. The double wall solves it properly, and it keeps the leaves cold for the whole service rather than the first half of it.
highlights: True double wall — no condensation ring, no doily
Holds chill through a full brunch service
Nests with the 3 L and 8 L sizes for storage
Hammered exterior option hides service marks
care: Dishwasher safe. Store inverted so the base cavity drains.

name: Copper Handi with Lid, 2 L
summary: The classic Indian serving handi, hammered copper outside and stainless inside. Goes from the pass to the table without a transfer.
story: A handi is the one piece on this list that is older than the hotel industry. The shape is unchanged because it works: the narrow mouth keeps a curry hot far longer than an open bowl, and the belly gives a ladle room to move. We have changed exactly one thing about it, which is the liner.
highlights: Stainless 304 lining — safe for acidic and dairy dishes
Narrow mouth holds heat far longer than an open bowl
Cast brass handles, riveted
Sizes 500 ml to 5 L
care: Hand wash. The liner is dishwasher-safe but the lacquered exterior is not.

name: Gravy Boat, 500 ml
summary: A 500 ml sauce boat with a drip-free lip and an underplate. It pours clean or it is not finished.
story: A sauce boat that dribbles is a laundry cost. The lip on this one is rolled to a specific radius and then hand-checked against a jug of water at the end of the line — every single piece, not a sample. It is the only 100% inspection on our floor and it exists because there is no way to fix a bad lip afterwards.
highlights: Every piece water-tested for a clean pour
Matching underplate included
Handle set clear of the pour line
Sizes 250 ml and 500 ml
care: Dishwasher safe.

name: Three-Tier Dessert & Fruit Stand
summary: A three-tier stand in graduated sizes. Halves the counter length a pastry display needs.
story: Counter space is the scarcest thing in a breakfast room. A three-tier stand puts the same number of pastries in a third of the footprint and, because it has height, it reads as a display rather than as storage.
highlights: Graduated 200 / 255 / 305 mm tiers
Knocks down for storage and washing
Threaded column, no wobble
Two-tier version available
care: Disassemble to wash. Do not over-tighten the finial — it is a brass thread.

name: Modular Buffet Riser Set (3 heights)
summary: Three graduated risers — 100, 150 and 200 mm — that turn a flat counter into a designed buffet.
story: The difference between a buffet that looks like a hotel and one that looks like a canteen is almost entirely height. Three risers under a twelve-metre line is a few thousand rupees; the alternative is a room that photographs badly at every wedding you host.
highlights: Graduated 100 / 150 / 200 mm — the proportion is the effect
Nest inside each other for storage
Non-slip feet, will not walk on a dressed counter
Rated to 25 kg each
care: Wipe down. Check foot pads at quarterly maintenance.

name: Brass Dome Cloche with Tray
summary: A spun brass cloche with a matching tray. Used for the reveal at the table and for the carry down a corridor.
story: A cloche has two jobs and they pull in opposite directions: it has to seal well enough to hold heat down a corridor, and it has to lift silently at the table. The rim is turned to a seat rather than left as a cut edge, which is what makes it do both.
highlights: Turned rim seat — seals warm, lifts silent
Matching tray, sold as a pair
Cast finial stays cool enough to handle
care: Hand wash. Dry the rim seat thoroughly or it will mark the tray.

name: Juice Dispenser with Steel Stand, 6 L
summary: A 6-litre dispenser on a stand with a stainless tap and an ice core. Replaces the jugs, and the labour of refilling them.
story: Jugs on a breakfast counter are a staffing decision disguised as a serving decision — somebody has to walk the floor refilling them for four hours. A dispenser holds three jugs' worth, guests serve themselves, and the ice core keeps it cold without diluting it.
highlights: Removable ice core — cold without dilution
Stainless tap, fully strippable for cleaning
Holds roughly three jugs; one refill per service
Drip tray included
care: Strip the tap weekly. A tap that is never stripped is the single most common health-audit finding on a breakfast counter.

name: Copper Cocktail Shaker, 750 ml
summary: A three-piece 750 ml shaker, copper outside and steel inside, with a built-in strainer that actually seals.
story: A shaker is handled at eye level eighteen inches from a paying guest, which makes it the most-looked-at object in a bar. It is also the one most likely to be dropped. The lining is drawn as one piece rather than seamed, because a seam is where a dropped shaker splits.
highlights: One-piece drawn steel lining — no seam to split
Integrated strainer, sealed cap
Copper never contacts the drink
Hammered or smooth
care: Rinse and dry immediately after each use. Citrus left in a shaker overnight will mark even a lined one.

name: Hammered Copper Water Pitcher, 1.5 L
summary: A 1.5-litre table pitcher, hammered and lined. The piece that sits on the table for the whole meal.
story: The pitcher stays on the table from the first guest to the last, which makes it the longest-serving object in the room and the one worth spending on. The lip is the same rolled-radius pour we use on the sauce boat, for the same reason.
highlights: Stainless lined — safe for citrus and long standing
Drip-free rolled lip, water-tested
Hammered face hides table marks
Matching tumblers available
care: Hand wash. Do not leave water standing overnight in a lacquered pitcher.
